executive_summary: This collection window (October 13-19, 2026) is the second full week after fashion month's close. Per instruction, this report did not assume a repeat of the prior window's thin finding and instead re-ran a genuine search across editorial, institutional, retail, and trade sources. Two items were confirmed: the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund's 2026 winner announcement, previously logged as scheduled for October 20, 2026 -- re-verified this window and confirmed still dated October 20, one day after this window closes, so it remains out-of-window context, not a loggable in-window signal, per this archive's no-forward-fill practice; and the British Fashion Council's LFW eligibility page, re-checked for a fourth consecutive window, which still shows no downstream reporting on the dropped wholesale-stockist requirement's effects. Given four consecutive silent windows (Sept 21, Oct 5, Oct 12, Oct 19) on that signal with no new corroborating or contradicting coverage, this report makes the independent call to retire lfw-wholesale-eligibility-dropped from active top_signals rather than carry it forward indefinitely -- see limitations for the reasoning and get_signal_status_history() for its full trend. No new, independently verifiable in-window garment, silhouette, or aesthetic discourse was found; Miami Fashion Week's October 13-17 dates fall inside this window but no dated, sourced runway or reaction coverage had surfaced as of search time, so it is not logged as a signal. On balance this window's honest read is again thin, reached by testing for new discourse and finding very little that met this archive's verification bar, not by assuming the prior window's outcome would repeat.
